description: Basic improvement on the chance of hitting the Weakpoint Monster's weak points.
Expert improvement on the chance of hitting the Weakpoint Monster's weak points.
The so-called walking dead are in fact alive.  They do not breathe and most do not eat, but their hearts still pump putrid blood to their rotting muscles, and if they bleed, they can be killed.
These twisted chimeras are each unique, yet follow a reliable set of underlying biological principles which can still be exploited.
Understanding of man-made armors and ways to exploit them.  You're able to find openings in certain kinds of body armor.
You're somewhat familiar with naturally armored creatures.  You're able to find openings in certain kinds of hardened shells and thick hides.
You're somewhat familiar with cybernetic creatures.  You're able to find openings and gaps that aren't as hardened.
Basic familiarity with various types of frogs and salamanders.
Basic familiarity with various types of birds.
Basic familiarity with various types of insects, arachnids, and worms.
Basic understanding of what's needed for certain creatures to fly, as well as ways of preventing it.
You're familiar with creatures presenting unsettling bones on their outer structure.
You have some practice in fighting large, hulking humanoids.  You're better at reaching certain weak points.

The bizarre pink monsters terrorizing the countryside are covered in a crusty outer shell which is quite strong but can crack when sufficient blunt force is applied, making them significantly more vulnerable to all attacks.  Knowing this, you're more likely to be able to be able to crack one open on purpose provided you are willing to get that close.

Mi-go appear to be composed entirely of a single type of tissue which can vary widely in density and hardness.  There aren't really distinct vital organs per se, but basic physics still apply, and you now know where their outer shells are weakest and their "bones" are thinnest.

There are a lot of parts of these giant carnivorous plants that don't do a lot of good in combat to attack and others that are too dense to easily harm, but any movable joint is a weak point you can disable with a well-placed strike.

All plants that move, be they sunflowers, venus flytraps, or giant man-eating monsters, operate on the same principle: hydraulics.  Lacking muscles, they use internal fluid pressure to extend or contract parts of their bodies.  Triffids have a specialized vascular system that allows them to do this very quickly and with a good deal of force, but this expanded xylem is vulnerable to attack, provided you know where it is, and at this point you have got a pretty good idea.
